rootCause: Two unrelated failures in one file. src/dashboard.ts declares `Widget` (with `id`/`label`) and `Gauge` (with `min`/`max`). `renderWidget` reads `w.title` and `w.caption`; `readGauge` reads `g.upper` and `g.lower`. The two interfaces share no member, no supertype and no usage — the only thing the four diagnostics have in common is the file they live in and the code TypeScript assigns them.
expectedFix: Two independent edits: read `label` in `renderWidget`, and read `min`/`max` in `readGauge`. Neither fix touches the other interface.
purpose: The harder negative control, sibling to `two-independent-roots`. That fixture separates two causes in two files with two different codes; this one puts two causes in ONE file under ONE code — TS2339 — the case where over-grouping is most tempting and, per §11, most destructive. §5.1 rule 3 (`same 2339 in the same file ⇒ one root`) is deliberately NOT applied, and this is its witness: each interface is misread twice, so a rule keyed on file+code would fold all four under a single header and hide one of the two bugs behind a counter. The engine instead keys on `declaredAt` and reports `4 errors · 1 file · 2 root causes` — Widget's two folded, Gauge's two folded, the two causes kept apart. Unlike `two-independent-roots` this fixture does fold within each cause, which is the point: it proves the split survives even when folding is active on both sides.
